A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AFL research work. All 15 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A-G, support comparison; no material gaps remain.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet, together with synthetic-data validation, ablations and appendix comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices D-G.

M1.justification: The specified aggregation coefficients receive a limited correction: the final terms in Eq. (8) change from minus to plus, and the inner signs in Eq. (10) change from plus to minus. These alter computed aggregation weights, while the backbone, local objectives, RI process and Algorithm 1 structure remain unchanged. Implementation changes or reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three image-classification datasets and synthetic dataset, with unchanged IID/non-IID, heterogeneity and client-count scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FedAvg, FedProx, MOON, FedGen, FedDyn, FedNTD and FedDisco. FedAvg participation in the partition and local-training comparisons is unchanged, and Appendix G retains FedFisher.

E3.justification: The reported partitions, backbone configurations, top-1 accuracy metric and training settings match. Appendix E retains 500 baseline communication rounds, one local epoch, batch size 64 and learning rate 0.05; Appendix G retains its 50-client comparison.

E4.justification: The client-count and heterogeneity analyses, RI ablation, backbone comparison, synthetic aggregation validation and local-versus-federated training analysis are retained without changed experiments or findings.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three runs for the main comparison and averages over five runs in Table A.1. No uncertainty-reporting or repeated-run information changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 and A.1-A.3 retain their numerical entries, and Figures 2-3 retain identical plots. For example, Table 1 still reports AFL accuracies of 80.75%, 58.56% and 54.67%; Table A.3 still reports FedFisher 19.31% versus AFL 35.87%.

T1.justification: Sign revisions substantively affect the correctness of the central MP-inverse and aggregation identities, rather than merely their notation. Eqs. (6), (8), (10) and corresponding derivations in Appendices A-C are revised while assumptions and theorem scope remain. However, v3 also changes the inner signs in (A.14) to plus, contradicting unchanged (A.10)-(A.11) and the expansion in (A.15).

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about closed-form AFL, one-epoch local training, single-round aggregation, RI and invariance to data partitioning and client number.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and stated limitations are unchanged, including reliance on a pretrained feature extractor, waiting for participating clients and restrictions associated with linear classifiers.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures, hyperparameter searches, RTX 4090 hardware, code-repository link and App Dummy.ipynb access instruction are unchanged. No additional reproducibility information accompanies the equation corrections.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and all 56 numbered references are retained, including the appendix discussion of FedFisher.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp changes from v2, 24 May 2025, to v3, 8 April 2026. The prose, terminology, headings and main-text/appendix organization otherwise match.

P2.justification: The three figures and seven tables retain their content arrangement, captions and locations. Page organization and equation placement remain unchanged; the mathematical sign revisions do not constitute a display redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the operative aggregation coefficients in (8) and (10) and associated RI derivation, improving the mathematical specification of the existing method. However, the newly incorrect plus signs in (A.14) conflict with (A.10)-(A.11), leaving the proof internally inconsistent. The corrected main formulas provide a net benefit, but the incomplete mathematical repair limits the overall improvement.
